entries.name: Authored scene event
entries.summary: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.

configuration.name: repeatable
configuration.limits: Required explicit value; challenge requires true.

limits: Choreography supports sequential moves, facing, three reaction cues and waits; no parallel groups or custom animation scripts.
Movement is limited to 128 steps and 4096 inspected cells per destination; waits to 5 seconds.
Scene event history is limited to 256 entries.

examples.intent: Run validated dialogue, rewards, flags, challenges and bounded actor choreography on interaction.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/scenes.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Resolve bounded actor actions and commit durable scene results before transient presentation.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.

details.conditions: Optional when condition evaluated through objective conditions.
details.actions: Dialogue, reward, flag, challenge, move, face, wait and react; challenge must be last. See docs/SCENE_ACTIONS.md for choreography limits.
details.rewards: Scene rewards accept coins, potions and orbs, not arbitrary inventory item IDs.
details.repetition: Explicit repeatable boolean; challenge events must be repeatable.
details.persistence: Non-repeatable events use saved map/event keys; rewards and flags commit before choreography and roll back if saving fails.

entries.name: Battle potion
entries.summary: Consume the configured battle potion in battle to heal the active companion by its pack-defined effect.
limits: Healing is capped at the companion's maximum HP and requires an available mapped supply.
Does not increase player speed or confer a three-battle buff.

examples.intent: Consume a potion in battle to apply the selected pack's healing effect.
examples.usage: Consult dist/src/domain/battle.js and reuse the existing definition.
examples.expected: Consume one mapped potion and heal the active companion according to its pack definition.

evidence.assertion: Regression coverage of the existing contract; this is not a new visual approval.

details.contexts: Battle action; no claim of an exploration-use interface.
details.consumption: Consumes one available potion on successful use.
details.strength: Pack-defined effect, capped by maximum HP.
details.stacking: Repeated uses heal again up to max HP; no buff stacking.
details.persistence: Remaining supplies and health use the existing battle/save transaction.

entries.name: Battle impact feedback
entries.summary: Show every resolved blow as a floating number, an eased HP bar with a trailing ghost, a held hit flash and a short scene shake, and play orb throws and victories as readable beats.
limits: Presentation only: it reads the already-resolved turn events and never changes damage, Focus, saves or outcomes.
Calm motion keeps the numbers and final bar widths but drops the shake, sparks and bar easing.
Each round now ends on a settled frame, so the foe's reply stays on screen for 500-700 ms (250 ms in calm motion) before controls return.

Capture beats are derived from the already-resolved throw: a success wobbles three times, a miss wobbles once more the closer it was (1 to 3), and calm motion collapses to a single wobble; the wobble count never changes the outcome.

Victory shows the foe fading, your friend hopping and the XP and coins the rules already granted; it adds about one second before the result screen, and a throw adds about two seconds (shorter in calm motion).

The pre-throw befriended status remains visible during throw/wobble; success is revealed when the orb settles and failure when it opens. Battle actions remain locked until playback ends, including calm motion.

examples.intent: Strike a wild creature and read the result at a glance.
examples.usage: Use Quick strike or the Element move; no configuration is needed.
examples.expected: A number floats over the target, the HP bar eases down while a pale ghost lags behind, and a heavier or super-effective hit shakes the scene harder.

examples.intent: Throw a capture orb at a weakened creature.
examples.usage: Press Capture orb (5) or click it; no configuration is needed.
examples.expected: The orb flies in and holds the creature, wobbles, then either settles with a star burst and floating rewards before the result screen, or opens and the creature pops back out.

evidence.assertion: Events map to floating numbers, tones, shake levels and heals without touching game state.
A real battle shows the strike and the foe's reply as floating numbers, bars ease, and calm motion removes the shake and sparks.

A real throw shows throw, three wobbles and settle with stars and floating rewards; a miss opens the orb and the creature pops out; a win fades the foe and floats XP; calm motion has no sparks and one wobble per throw.

details.trigger: A resolved strike, enemy attack, riposte, potion, charge recovery, orb throw or win event.
details.inputs: The turn event (damage, effectiveness, action kind, healed amount) and the per-frame HP snapshot.
details.sequence: Each frame draws the bars from the previous frame's width, forces a reflow and sets the new width so the transition runs; numbers rise for 0.9 s; the scene shakes at level 1 or 2. Orb throws expand into throw, wobble and settle-or-open beats; a win adds a victory beat where the foe fades out.
details.results: Damage, healing and effectiveness read without parsing the battle log; numbers are hidden from assistive technology because the log already announces them.
details.cancellation: A new frame replaces the markup; leaving the battle or skipping playback drops pending effects.
details.errors: With no previous width (first frame or a switched companion) the bar is drawn at its final value without easing.
details.persistence: Presentation-only; nothing is saved.

configuration.name: --species / --strict-source-grid / --check / --preview-dir
configuration.limits: Select a species, reject crowded new sources, verify without mutation and inspect raw/segmented/anchored/runtime stages. All selected inputs preflight before writes.

limits: Legacy recovery preserves original foreground pixels before fitting; it cannot invent missing anatomy or repair a different creature design.
Indexed species keep their existing no-dither palette conversion.
The spacing audit verifies hashes, clear margins and baselines; visual review at gameplay scale remains separate from owner taste.

examples.intent: Review a newly generated Emberkin combat sheet without replacing runtime art.

evidence.assertion: Nonuniform rows, thin tails, detached particles, alpha holes, pixel conservation, shared scale, transparent gutters and 360 combat frames.
Exact runtime hashes and margin/baseline audit for 40 atlases and 1,160 cells.
Recorded complete-pose review at 115 px, pinned to current outputs and contact sheet; owner taste remains pending.

details.trigger: Authoring or verifying a creature combat source sheet.

details.cancellation: --check never writes outputs; invalid input stops before staging.
details.errors: Missing bodies, invalid boundaries, inadequate new-source gutters or output mismatch fail with diagnostics.
details.persistence: Changes source/output provenance and authoring evidence only; no game save or combat rule changes.

entries.name: Guardian counterplay rewards
entries.summary: Show the next guardian action and matchup-based damage, then reward a valid tactical response when the fight is won.
limits: Damage is a random-roll range for the current active companion; switching changes the matchup and forecast.

examples.intent: Read a guardian's next action, compare current and Guard damage, and choose a response before its turn.

details.trigger: While a guardian battle is idle, the interface previews its next tactic action and any relevant response window.
details.inputs: The deterministic tactic pattern position, species damage formula, current active matchup, Guard factor, Focus, party health and configured response conditions.
details.sequence: Derive the upcoming action, unguarded and guarded random damage ranges, brace or charge effects and matching responses without mutating battle state. The existing resolver independently records only qualifying player actions and pays recorded bonuses on victory.
details.results: The battle panel explains whether the guardian acts after the player's choice, the current ally's damage range, Guard reduction/riposte, Focus cost, next brace/charge consequence, and any available response reward.
details.cancellation: The forecast is hidden while an action resolves or the battle ends. A lost or abandoned fight pays no response bonus; a saved interrupted fight retains recorded responses. A response requiring the guardian's next action is not recorded if the player's action defeats it first.
details.errors: Unknown response IDs in a saved battle are discarded during normalization.
details.persistence: The forecast is derived and adds no save fields. Recorded response IDs remain part of the existing battle checkpoint and compatible with older saves.

entries.name: Responsive playfield and readable name tags
entries.summary: On desktop the game frame fits the window height and renders more of the world in wider windows; character and landmark name tags are drawn on top, outlined and kept apart.
limits: Desktop layout only (width 1000 px or more, height 540 px or more); phones and small windows keep the existing 3:2 frame at 960 px of world width.

details.trigger: Window resize, fullscreen change or first load.
details.inputs: The canvas bounding box and the 960/1800 pixel width limits.
details.sequence: resize() sets the canvas width to one pixel per CSS pixel above 960 and derives the height from the box; the renderer already reads canvas.width and canvas.height every frame, so visible tiles and objects follow. Labels are collected during the object pass and drawn afterwards, farthest first.
details.results: More world on large screens, no vertical scrolling to reach controls, and name tags that stay legible over foliage.
details.cancellation: Not applicable.
details.errors: A zero-size box (hidden tab) leaves the previous canvas size untouched.
details.persistence: Nothing is saved; the Zoom setting keeps its existing storage.
